## Can quantum computing make a measurable difference for optimization problems in health and biology?

BENQODHI is a European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) exploratory activity.
It brings together experts in quantum computing, optimisation, AI, biology and health
to define credible, open benchmarks for transparent comparison across quantum, hybrid,
AI, and classical approaches.

The project is organised around three goals:

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 01 / Focus
**Make the questions real.**
Optimization challenges rooted in health and biology — not generic combinatorial
problems dressed in biological vocabulary.
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 02 / Method
**Make comparisons fair.**
Instances, baselines, metrics and resource accounting that let classical, AI-based,
hybrid and quantum methods be compared on equal terms.
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
### 03 / Outcome
**Make evidence reusable.**
A practical pathway toward open benchmark resources the community can build on.
:::

:::

## Origin: the BENQODHI workshop

The project's first milestone is the **BENQODHI Workshop**, 10–11 September 2026 at
JRC Ispra, Italy. The workshop convenes invited speakers and contributors to sketch a
first set of candidate benchmark problems and a shared framework for building them out.

[More about the workshop →](workshop.qmd)

## Get involved

Problem proposals, suggestions and ideas are welcome from anyone, not only workshop
participants.

[How to contribute →](contribute.qmd)
